mike_w: Ran an apples-to-apples run comparing chunked streaming vs bulk non-streaming on rtx-pool-A. Using synthetic replay harness with 12 concurrent clients, seq=1024, model=rw-gg-13b-quant. Streaming median ~72ms/token p95 210ms/token; non-streaming median ~65ms/token p95 180ms/token. But end-to-end app latency seems worse for streaming due to client readloop backpressure. Anyone seen this pattern?

bench-bot: Attached CSV summary and quick stats. Command used: `./harness --replay --clients 12 --streaming --chunk-size 256 --kv-cache=enabled --adaptive-batching=on`

jess: Did you pin the kernel selector? I.e., `kernel=fused-attn` vs `kernel=auto` can flip based on chunk size. Small chunks often fall back to matmul path.

mike_w: I left kernel=auto. Profile shows a kernel-selection flip at seq threshold ~128. Chunk-size 512 picks fused-attn; 256 falls back to matmul-fallback.

raj: For apples-to-apples we should: 1) pre-warm KV cache with 10k tokens, 2) disable adaptive batching (fixed batch=8), 3) ensure identical inter-arrival distributions between synthetic and replay. Otherwise batching heuristics differ and you don't compare the same thing.

anya: FYI, I observed KV hit-rate drops (~18%) in streaming runs when chunking enabled. Suspect partial frames from readloop are causing early prefix eviction (server sees incomplete prefix and GC).

mike_w: Reproducer: setting the client readloop to read 128B frames caused many partial chunks and we saw prefix evictions. Switching to a 4k read frame reduced evictions and improved p95. Stack hint: `readloop.v2` recently changed how it signals frame-complete, might correlate.

bench-bot: Flame profile snapshot: CPU breakdown: io_readloop 23%, batch_pack 14%, kv_lookup 12%, kernel_select 9%, kernel_exec 28%.

jess: kernel_select at 9% is higher than I'd expect. Let's cache kernel choice per (model, seq_dist, chunk_size) combination in the serving process to avoid run-time selection overhead for stable traffic.

raj: Also observed non-deterministic p95 spikes on Dedicated due to occasional compaction pauses during peak loads. Posting heapprofile: http://internal/heap/1782/compaction-heap.pb — compaction aligned with p95 spikes.

mike_w: Proposed plan: 1) run controlled apples-to-apples with fixed batch and KV pre-warm, 2) add readloop frame-size and prefix_evictions metric to harness, 3) test kernel-cache patch (PR#4521) to remove kernel_select overhead. Who can own kernel-cache bench?

anya: I'll pick up kernel-cache bench and add a `--kv-warmup` flag to the harness so pre-warm is reproducible. Will run both streaming and non-streaming with identical arrival profiles.

jess: :thumbsup: I will review PR#4521 once you have bench outputs. Also add a lightweight smoke that fails CI if streaming readloop shows prefix_evictions > 1% after warmup.

bench-bot: :white_check_mark: scheduled job `bench-apples-178201-next` at 1782013000. Results will be stored at `/bench/results/178201/stream-vs-bulk/` and CSVs plus flamegraphs will be uploaded.

deploy-bot: Heads-up: runtime v0.53 deploying to staging in ~1h. If bench runs need staging-specific flags, coordinate now.

mike_w: Thanks everyone. If you have quick tips for reproducing p95 spikes in non-streaming (Dedicated) ping me. Will follow up with bench outputs and a short writeup. Closing thread for now.
